device_functions.function_name: Read chip identification
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: device has completed power-on-reset (POR) after VDD and VDDIO reach minimum levels. Execution: host reads register 0xD0. Register side-effects: read-only, no side effects. Result: returns chip_id (expected 0x60 for BME280). Use-case: verify communications and correct device present. Completion: immediate upon successful read. Error conditions: if read returns different value or read fails, treat as communication error or wrong device. Recommended: perform as first step after POR and before other configuration or measurements.

device_functions.function_name: Soft reset (power-on-reset sequence)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: accessible via interface (I2C or SPI). Execution: write value 0xB6 to reset register 0xE0. Register state changes: device performs full power-on-reset procedure; reset register read always returns 0x00. Side-effects: all registers return to POR default states; internal NVM trimming will be copied to image registers (im_update will be set while copying). Device enters sleep mode after reset. Timing: copying and POR settle times—soft reset wait recommended 2 ms in self-test; full settling is guaranteed after internal copy completes (im_update bit cleared). Error conditions: writing other values to 0xE0 has no effect. Note: cycling VDD also performs POR; cycling VDDIO alone does not reset device.

device_functions.function_name: Read calibration/trimming parameters
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: device in any mode (registers accessible in sleep and other modes); NVM image copy may be taking place after POR (check status.im_update). Execution: burst-read the calibration address ranges 0x88..0xA1 and 0xE1..0xE7. Register state changes: read-only, no side-effects. Details: calibration words must be assembled from multiple 8-bit registers: dig_T1..dig_T3 (0x88..0x8D), dig_P1..dig_P9 (0x8E..0x9F), dig_H1 (0xA1), dig_H2..dig_H6 (0xE1..0xE7) with H4/H5 spanning nibbles across 0xE4/0xE5/0xE6. Data format: 16-bit words are little-endian pairs; some are signed two's-complement. Use these exact values for compensation formulas. Timing: copying from NVM to image registers occurs at POR and before conversions; wait until status.im_update==0 to ensure stable trimming values. Error conditions: reading during im_update may return intermediate values; recommended to wait for im_update clear.

device_functions.function_name: Configure humidity oversampling
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must set ctrl_hum (0xF2) and then write ctrl_meas (0xF4) for the humidity oversampling change to take effect. Execution steps: write osrs_h[2:0] into ctrl_hum (0xF2[2:0]) to select skipped/×1/×2/×4/×8/×16. Immediately after, write ctrl_meas (0xF4) (even if unchanged) to apply the new humidity setting. Register state changes: ctrl_hum (0xF2) is updated by host; change becomes active when ctrl_meas write occurs. Resulting behavior: humidity measurement enabled/disabled or oversampling adjusted; when skipped, humidity output registers return 0x8000. Side-effects: writing ctrl_hum alone does not change measurement until ctrl_meas is written; multiple writes to ctrl_hum while a mode transition is pending may be ignored. Completion conditions: new humidity setting active after ctrl_meas write completes and device completes any ongoing conversion. Error conditions: writes to ctrl_hum are ignored until ctrl_meas write; if device currently performing a conversion, mode/oversampling changes are delayed until conversion end (status.measuring set).

device_functions.function_name: Configure temperature & pressure oversampling and select sensor mode (sleep/forced/normal)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: device accessible and not in the middle of a conversion if immediate mode change is required (check status.measuring). Execution steps: write osrs_t[2:0] and osrs_p[2:0] into ctrl_meas (0xF4[7:2]) to set temperature and pressure oversampling. Then set mode[1:0] in ctrl_meas (0xF4[1:0]) to choose: 00 = sleep, 01/10 = forced, 11 = normal. For humidity changes previously written to ctrl_hum, a write to ctrl_meas is required to apply them. Behavior: - Sleep: no measurements, lowest power. - Forced: initiates a single measurement sequence (temperature, pressure, humidity if enabled) according to oversampling and filter; after measurement completes, device returns to sleep and data are available in data registers. - Normal: device cycles measurements and standby periods automatically; standby duration is set by config.t_sb. Side-effects: starting forced/normal mode while a measurement is active is delayed until current conversion completes. Mode transitions are serialized: further mode changes or ctrl_hum writes are ignored until transition done. Completion/waiting: measurement active while status.measuring==1; for forced mode host must poll measuring bit or wait t_measure (see measurement time formula). Error conditions: invalid osrs values treated as highest supported (×16) per table; if pressure or temperature oversampling is 000 (skipped) and their data are requested, outputs are set to 0x80000. Recommended: for synchronized low-rate reads use forced mode; for filtering use normal mode.

device_functions.function_name: Configure IIR filter, standby time and 3-wire SPI enable
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: writes to config (0xF5) in normal mode may be ignored; perform writes while in sleep mode for guaranteed effect. Execution: set t_sb[2:0] (0xF5[7:5]) to choose standby interval in normal mode (0.5 ms ... 1000 ms or special values 10/20 ms) and filter[2:0] (0xF5[4:2]) to choose IIR filter coefficient (off,2,4,8,16). Set spi3w_en (0xF5[0]) to '1' to enable 3-wire SPI mode. Register side-effects: writing filter resets filter memory (next ADC values pass through unchanged and become initial memory). Behavior: filter slows response and increases effective resolution for pressure and temperature to 20-bit when enabled; standby time defines inactive period between measurements in normal mode and affects ODR. Timing/notes: filter coefficients map to samples-to-75%-response (see table); changing filter resets internal filter memory — if temporary re-initialization desired write filter register to reinitialize. Error conditions: writes may be ignored in normal mode; recommended to switch to sleep before writing to ensure deterministic update.

device_functions.function_name: Burst read raw measurements (pressure, temperature, humidity) with data shadowing
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: prefer burst read (I2C or SPI) starting at 0xF7 for consistent snapshot; in normal mode measurements may update while reading so burst read is required for shadowing to guarantee consistency. Execution: - For pressure+temperature read bytes 0xF7..0xFC (or 0xF7..0xF9/0xFA..0xFC depending on needed data). - For humidity include 0xFD..0xFE. Data format: pressure and temperature are unsigned 20-bit values assembled from MSB, LSB, and XLSB nibbles (up[19:12]=0xF7, up[11:4]=0xF8, up[3:0]=0xF9[7:4]); temperature ut uses 0xFA..0xFC similarly; humidity is unsigned 16-bit uh formed from 0xFD (msb) and 0xFE (lsb). Shadowing: if a new measurement finishes while host is reading, new results are copied into shadow registers and will replace data registers only at end of burst read (CS rising for SPI or STOP condition for I2C). Side-effects: reading unused registers is faster than multiple small reads; recommended to do single burst reads to avoid inconsistent cross-sample mixing. Timing: reading is immediate; ensure host reads within constraints of interface timings. Error conditions: reading outside burst or using multiple sequential reads may return inconsistent multi-parameter sets when operating in normal mode.

device_functions.function_name: Read device status bits (measuring, im_update)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: none. Execution: read status register 0xF3. Register semantics: - measuring (0xF3[3]) is '1' whenever a conversion is running and '0' when results have been transferred to data registers. - im_update (0xF3[0]) is '1' while NVM trimming parameters are being copied to image registers (occurs at POR and before conversions) and '0' when copy finished. Use: poll measuring to know when measurement is complete (forced mode) or to detect safe times to change modes or ctrl_hum. Poll im_update after POR or reset to avoid reading calibration image while copying. Side-effects: read-only; no side-effects. Completion: when measuring==0 and im_update==0 device ready for writes/reads. Error: ignoring these bits may lead to race conditions (e.g., lost ctrl_hum update or inconsistent calibration usage).

device_functions.function_name: Compensate raw ADC to physical units (temperature, pressure, humidity)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must have read raw ADC values (20-bit pressure/temp, 16-bit humidity) from data registers and read trimming parameters (dig_*). Execution: compute compensated values using recommended formulas and intermediate t_fine. Temperature: compute t_fine from adc_T and dig_T1..T3; returns temperature (0.01°C resolution). Pressure: uses t_fine and dig_P1..P9; best accuracy requires 64-bit integer or double precision floating point; guard against var1==0 to avoid division by zero (return 0). Pressure output format: Q24.8 fixed point or Pa in double. Humidity: computed using t_fine and dig_H1..H6 with saturation and bounds (0..100% RH). Side-effects: no register writes; local software state variable t_fine must be retained between compensation calls for pressure/humidity. Error conditions: insufficient precision (32-bit alternative reduces accuracy and may add noise at high filter levels). Implementation notes: recommended to use Bosch API; if implementing, follow exact fixed-point sequences; check for over/underflow and saturate humidity to [0,100].

device_functions.function_name: Self-test flow (communication, bond-wire, and plausibility checks)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must provide read/write/delay primitives. Execution sequence: 1) perform soft reset by writing 0xB6 to reset (0xE0) and wait ~2 ms; 2) read id (0xD0) and validate chip id==0x60; 3) read trimming parameters (0x88..0xA1, 0xE1..0xE7) and verify ranges; 4) configure sensor for a measurement (write ctrl_hum and ctrl_meas) and trigger a forced measurement, wait up to 7 ms for conversion (or poll status.measuring); 5) read uncompensated ADC and check for clipping to min/max ADC values (bond-wire test); 6) compute compensated temperature and pressure and compare against user-defined plausibility limits (e.g., 0..40°C, 900..1100 hPa). Register effects: writes to reset and ctrl_meas/ctrl_hum as part of test; reads from id, status, data, and calibration. Timing: total wait ~9 ms (2 ms reset + 7 ms conversion) plus communication time (dependent on interface speed). Return codes: defined codes for comm error, trimming out-of-bound, bond-wire failure, implausible temperature/pressure/humidity. Error semantics: tests performed in ascending code order; on first failing test the routine returns that code and stops further tests.

device_functions.function_name: Calculate measurement time, ODR and current consumption
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must know oversampling settings in ctrl_meas (osrs_t, osrs_p) and ctrl_hum (osrs_h) and t_sb in config. Execution: compute active measurement time using t_measure,typ and t_measure,max formulas: t_measure,typ = 1 + [2*T_oversampling]_{t!=0} + [2*P_oversampling + 0.5]_{p!=0} + [2*H_oversampling + 0.5]_{h!=0} (ms). Maximum similar with 2.3 factors. In forced mode max ODR = 1000 / t_measure. In normal mode ODR = 1000 / (t_measure + t_standby) where t_standby from config.t_sb. Current: compute I_DD,forced or I_DD,normal using formulas using I_DDSL, I_DDSB and per-measurement currents I_DDT, I_DDP, I_DDH multiplied by oversampling factors (see doc). Register dependencies: ctrl_meas (0xF4), ctrl_hum (0xF2), config.t_sb (0xF5[7:5]). Result: numerical ODR and expected average current consumption, used for power budgeting. Error semantics: t_standby accuracy subject to Δt_standby specification; actual current varies with temperature and oversampling selection.

device_functions.function_name: Interface selection and SPI/I²C access semantics
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: physical CSB and SDO pin wiring determines active interface. Behavior: - If CSB tied to VDDIO the I²C interface is active. If CSB pulled low (asserted) the SPI interface becomes active and the device disables I²C until next POR. - SDO pin logic level selects LSB of I2C 7-bit address: SDO=GND -> 0x76, SDO=VDDIO -> 0x77; SDO must not be left floating. SPI specifics: MSB of SPI control byte is RW (1 for read, 0 for write); SPI register address uses 7 LSBs (i.e., SPI transfers use reg_addr without bit7) and auto-increment during multi-byte read/writes. 3-wire SPI is enabled by setting spi3w_en in config (0xF5[0]). I²C semantics: before reading, write register address in write mode then issue repeated-start and read; multi-byte reads auto-increment register address. Side-effects: pulling CSB low once locks device into SPI mode until POR. Timing: follow interface timing constraints in datasheet. Error conditions: leaving interface pins high when VDDIO is off can damage device via ESD diodes; ensure proper power sequencing. Note: spi3w_en controlled at config (0xF5) affects SDI/SDO pin behavior.

targets.rejection_summary: readCalibration() decodes calibration bytes using an incorrect buffer index for dig_H1, causing an out-of-bounds access and incorrect humidity calibration (dig_H1).

rejected_sections.rejection_reason: The calibration decode routine reads the 0x88..0xA1 block into buf1 but uses buf1[0x1A] to obtain dig_H1. The offset of register 0xA1 relative to 0x88 is 0x19, not 0x1A, so buf1[0x1A] is out-of-range for the allocated buffer and results in incorrect dig_H1 value and a potential memory corruption.

rejected_functions.rejection_reason: Uses buf1[0x1A] to read dig_H1 after reading 0x88..0xA1 into buf1. The correct index for 0xA1 in the buf1 array is 0xA1 - 0x88 = 0x19 (decimal 25). This causes an off-by-one/out-of-bounds error and incorrect calibration decoding for humidity.

rejection_reasons.description: Calibration decoding contains an off-by-one buffer index for dig_H1 (buf1[0x1A] instead of buf1[0x19]) leading to out-of-bounds access and wrong humidity calibration.

semantic_result.feedback:
Found one blocking semantic defect in the candidate implementation that must be fixed before further verification.

1) Critical bug — calibration buffer index (driver_source_01::readCalibration):
- Problem: After reading registers 0x88..0xA1 into buf1, the code reads dig_H1 from buf1[0x1A]. The offset of register 0xA1 relative to 0x88 is 0xA1 - 0x88 = 0x19 (decimal 25). buf1 has indices 0..25, so buf1[0x1A] (26) is out-of-bounds.
- Effect: Out-of-bounds read / memory corruption and wrong dig_H1 value. This will break humidity compensation and can destabilize the driver.
- Fix: Use buf1[0x19] (or compute index = 0xA1 - 0x88) to read dig_H1. Also ensure buffer lengths and index calculations are correct and documented.

2) Suggested additional checks and hardening (for the next coder iteration):
- Add bounds-safe index calculations or static assertions for expected buffer sizes (e.g., compute offsets as register - start_register and assert within buffer length).
- Add a small validation step after decoding calibration (e.g., sanity checks on extracted calibration ranges or a flag indicating calibration completeness) so begin()/readCalibration() can return CalibrationMissing if data look invalid.
- Add unit tests or table-driven tests for calibration decoding using known sample bytes to catch similar off-by-one errors.
- Run static analysis or address sanitizer (if available on host) to detect out-of-bounds stack accesses.

3) Non-blocking notes (passed aspects worth keeping):
- The driver correctly implements I2C repeated-start reads, SPI RW/address control-byte semantics, uses caller-owned TwoWire/SPIClass (does not call Wire.begin()/SPI.begin()), polls status.im_update, applies 2 ms reset delay, uses burst read 0xF7..0xFE, and implements Bosch compensation algorithms with appropriate integer/64-bit math and saturation.

After the calibration index bug is fixed and the calibration decode validated, re-run semantic verification focusing on: exact calibration field values (dig_H1..H6), sign-extension for H4/H5, and correct behavior when calibration image is unstable (im_update).

device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: device has completed power-on-reset (POR) after VDD and VDDIO reach minimum levels. Execution: host reads register 0xD0. Register side-effects: read-only, no side effects. Result: returns chip_id (expected 0x60 for BME280). Use-case: verify communications and correct device present. Completion: immediate upon successful read. Error conditions: if read returns different value or read fails, treat as communication error or wrong device. Recommended: perform as first step after POR and before other configuration or measurements.

device_functions.function_name: Soft reset (power-on-reset sequence)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: accessible via interface (I2C or SPI). Execution: write value 0xB6 to reset register 0xE0. Register state changes: device performs full power-on-reset procedure; reset register read always returns 0x00. Side-effects: all registers return to POR default states; internal NVM trimming will be copied to image registers (im_update will be set while copying). Device enters sleep mode after reset. Timing: copying and POR settle times—soft reset wait recommended 2 ms in self-test; full settling is guaranteed after internal copy completes (im_update bit cleared). Error conditions: writing other values to 0xE0 has no effect. Note: cycling VDD also performs POR; cycling VDDIO alone does not reset device.

device_functions.function_name: Read calibration/trimming parameters
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: device in any mode (registers accessible in sleep and other modes); NVM image copy may be taking place after POR (check status.im_update). Execution: burst-read the calibration address ranges 0x88..0xA1 and 0xE1..0xE7. Register state changes: read-only, no side-effects. Details: calibration words must be assembled from multiple 8-bit registers: dig_T1..dig_T3 (0x88..0x8D), dig_P1..dig_P9 (0x8E..0x9F), dig_H1 (0xA1), dig_H2..dig_H6 (0xE1..0xE7) with H4/H5 spanning nibbles across 0xE4/0xE5/0xE6. Data format: 16-bit words are little-endian pairs; some are signed two's-complement. Use these exact values for compensation formulas. Timing: copying from NVM to image registers occurs at POR and before conversions; wait until status.im_update==0 to ensure stable trimming values. Error conditions: reading during im_update may return intermediate values; recommended to wait for im_update clear.

device_functions.function_name: Configure humidity oversampling
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must set ctrl_hum (0xF2) and then write ctrl_meas (0xF4) for the humidity oversampling change to take effect. Execution steps: write osrs_h[2:0] into ctrl_hum (0xF2[2:0]) to select skipped/×1/×2/×4/×8/×16. Immediately after, write ctrl_meas (0xF4) (even if unchanged) to apply the new humidity setting. Register state changes: ctrl_hum (0xF2) is updated by host; change becomes active when ctrl_meas write occurs. Resulting behavior: humidity measurement enabled/disabled or oversampling adjusted; when skipped, humidity output registers return 0x8000. Side-effects: writing ctrl_hum alone does not change measurement until ctrl_meas is written; multiple writes to ctrl_hum while a mode transition is pending may be ignored. Completion conditions: new humidity setting active after ctrl_meas write completes and device completes any ongoing conversion. Error conditions: writes to ctrl_hum are ignored until ctrl_meas write; if device currently performing a conversion, mode/oversampling changes are delayed until conversion end (status.measuring set).

device_functions.function_name: Configure temperature & pressure oversampling and select sensor mode (sleep/forced/normal)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: device accessible and not in the middle of a conversion if immediate mode change is required (check status.measuring). Execution steps: write osrs_t[2:0] and osrs_p[2:0] into ctrl_meas (0xF4[7:2]) to set temperature and pressure oversampling. Then set mode[1:0] in ctrl_meas (0xF4[1:0]) to choose: 00 = sleep, 01/10 = forced, 11 = normal. For humidity changes previously written to ctrl_hum, a write to ctrl_meas is required to apply them. Behavior: - Sleep: no measurements, lowest power. - Forced: initiates a single measurement sequence (temperature, pressure, humidity if enabled) according to oversampling and filter; after measurement completes, device returns to sleep and data are available in data registers. - Normal: device cycles measurements and standby periods automatically; standby duration is set by config.t_sb. Side-effects: starting forced/normal mode while a measurement is active is delayed until current conversion completes. Mode transitions are serialized: further mode changes or ctrl_hum writes are ignored until transition done. Completion/waiting: measurement active while status.measuring==1; for forced mode host must poll measuring bit or wait t_measure (see measurement time formula). Error conditions: invalid osrs values treated as highest supported (×16) per table; if pressure or temperature oversampling is 000 (skipped) and their data are requested, outputs are set to 0x80000. Recommended: for synchronized low-rate reads use forced mode; for filtering use normal mode.

device_functions.function_name: Configure IIR filter, standby time and 3-wire SPI enable
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: writes to config (0xF5) in normal mode may be ignored; perform writes while in sleep mode for guaranteed effect. Execution: set t_sb[2:0] (0xF5[7:5]) to choose standby interval in normal mode (0.5 ms ... 1000 ms or special values 10/20 ms) and filter[2:0] (0xF5[4:2]) to choose IIR filter coefficient (off,2,4,8,16). Set spi3w_en (0xF5[0]) to '1' to enable 3-wire SPI mode. Register side-effects: writing filter resets filter memory (next ADC values pass through unchanged and become initial memory). Behavior: filter slows response and increases effective resolution for pressure and temperature to 20-bit when enabled; standby time defines inactive period between measurements in normal mode and affects ODR. Timing/notes: filter coefficients map to samples-to-75%-response (see table); changing filter resets internal filter memory — if temporary re-initialization desired write filter register to reinitialize. Error conditions: writes may be ignored in normal mode; recommended to switch to sleep before writing to ensure deterministic update.

device_functions.function_name: Burst read raw measurements (pressure, temperature, humidity) with data shadowing
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: prefer burst read (I2C or SPI) starting at 0xF7 for consistent snapshot; in normal mode measurements may update while reading so burst read is required for shadowing to guarantee consistency. Execution: - For pressure+temperature read bytes 0xF7..0xFC (or 0xF7..0xF9/0xFA..0xFC depending on needed data). - For humidity include 0xFD..0xFE. Data format: pressure and temperature are unsigned 20-bit values assembled from MSB, LSB, and XLSB nibbles (up[19:12]=0xF7, up[11:4]=0xF8, up[3:0]=0xF9[7:4]); temperature ut uses 0xFA..0xFC similarly; humidity is unsigned 16-bit uh formed from 0xFD (msb) and 0xFE (lsb). Shadowing: if a new measurement finishes while host is reading, new results are copied into shadow registers and will replace data registers only at end of burst read (CS rising for SPI or STOP condition for I2C). Side-effects: reading unused registers is faster than multiple small reads; recommended to do single burst reads to avoid inconsistent cross-sample mixing. Timing: reading is immediate; ensure host reads within constraints of interface timings. Error conditions: reading outside burst or using multiple sequential reads may return inconsistent multi-parameter sets when operating in normal mode.

device_functions.function_name: Read device status bits (measuring, im_update)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: none. Execution: read status register 0xF3. Register semantics: - measuring (0xF3[3]) is '1' whenever a conversion is running and '0' when results have been transferred to data registers. - im_update (0xF3[0]) is '1' while NVM trimming parameters are being copied to image registers (occurs at POR and before conversions) and '0' when copy finished. Use: poll measuring to know when measurement is complete (forced mode) or to detect safe times to change modes or ctrl_hum. Poll im_update after POR or reset to avoid reading calibration image while copying. Side-effects: read-only; no side-effects. Completion: when measuring==0 and im_update==0 device ready for writes/reads. Error: ignoring these bits may lead to race conditions (e.g., lost ctrl_hum update or inconsistent calibration usage).

device_functions.function_name: Compensate raw ADC to physical units (temperature, pressure, humidity)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must have read raw ADC values (20-bit pressure/temp, 16-bit humidity) from data registers and read trimming parameters (dig_*). Execution: compute compensated values using recommended formulas and intermediate t_fine. Temperature: compute t_fine from adc_T and dig_T1..T3; returns temperature (0.01°C resolution). Pressure: uses t_fine and dig_P1..P9; best accuracy requires 64-bit integer or double precision floating point; guard against var1==0 to avoid division by zero (return 0). Pressure output format: Q24.8 fixed point or Pa in double. Humidity: computed using t_fine and dig_H1..H6 with saturation and bounds (0..100% RH). Side-effects: no register writes; local software state variable t_fine must be retained between compensation calls for pressure/humidity. Error conditions: insufficient precision (32-bit alternative reduces accuracy and may add noise at high filter levels). Implementation notes: recommended to use Bosch API; if implementing, follow exact fixed-point sequences; check for over/underflow and saturate humidity to [0,100].

device_functions.function_name: Self-test flow (communication, bond-wire, and plausibility checks)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must provide read/write/delay primitives. Execution sequence: 1) perform soft reset by writing 0xB6 to reset (0xE0) and wait ~2 ms; 2) read id (0xD0) and validate chip id==0x60; 3) read trimming parameters (0x88..0xA1, 0xE1..0xE7) and verify ranges; 4) configure sensor for a measurement (write ctrl_hum and ctrl_meas) and trigger a forced measurement, wait up to 7 ms for conversion (or poll status.measuring); 5) read uncompensated ADC and check for clipping to min/max ADC values (bond-wire test); 6) compute compensated temperature and pressure and compare against user-defined plausibility limits (e.g., 0..40°C, 900..1100 hPa). Register effects: writes to reset and ctrl_meas/ctrl_hum as part of test; reads from id, status, data, and calibration. Timing: total wait ~9 ms (2 ms reset + 7 ms conversion) plus communication time (dependent on interface speed). Return codes: defined codes for comm error, trimming out-of-bound, bond-wire failure, implausible temperature/pressure/humidity. Error semantics: tests performed in ascending code order; on first failing test the routine returns that code and stops further tests.

device_functions.function_name: Calculate measurement time, ODR and current consumption
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must know oversampling settings in ctrl_meas (osrs_t, osrs_p) and ctrl_hum (osrs_h) and t_sb in config. Execution: compute active measurement time using t_measure,typ and t_measure,max formulas: t_measure,typ = 1 + [2*T_oversampling]_{t!=0} + [2*P_oversampling + 0.5]_{p!=0} + [2*H_oversampling + 0.5]_{h!=0} (ms). Maximum similar with 2.3 factors. In forced mode max ODR = 1000 / t_measure. In normal mode ODR = 1000 / (t_measure + t_standby) where t_standby from config.t_sb. Current: compute I_DD,forced or I_DD,normal using formulas using I_DDSL, I_DDSB and per-measurement currents I_DDT, I_DDP, I_DDH multiplied by oversampling factors (see doc). Register dependencies: ctrl_meas (0xF4), ctrl_hum (0xF2), config.t_sb (0xF5[7:5]). Result: numerical ODR and expected average current consumption, used for power budgeting. Error semantics: t_standby accuracy subject to Δt_standby specification; actual current varies with temperature and oversampling selection.

device_functions.function_name: Interface selection and SPI/I²C access semantics
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: physical CSB and SDO pin wiring determines active interface. Behavior: - If CSB tied to VDDIO the I²C interface is active. If CSB pulled low (asserted) the SPI interface becomes active and the device disables I²C until next POR. - SDO pin logic level selects LSB of I2C 7-bit address: SDO=GND -> 0x76, SDO=VDDIO -> 0x77; SDO must not be left floating. SPI specifics: MSB of SPI control byte is RW (1 for read, 0 for write); SPI register address uses 7 LSBs (i.e., SPI transfers use reg_addr without bit7) and auto-increment during multi-byte read/writes. 3-wire SPI is enabled by setting spi3w_en in config (0xF5[0]). I²C semantics: before reading, write register address in write mode then issue repeated-start and read; multi-byte reads auto-increment register address. Side-effects: pulling CSB low once locks device into SPI mode until POR. Timing: follow interface timing constraints in datasheet. Error conditions: leaving interface pins high when VDDIO is off can damage device via ESD diodes; ensure proper power sequencing. Note: spi3w_en controlled at config (0xF5) affects SDI/SDO pin behavior.

device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: prefer burst read (I2C or SPI) starting at 0xF7 for consistent snapshot; in normal mode measurements may update while reading so burst read is required for shadowing to guarantee consistency. Execution: - For pressure+temperature read bytes 0xF7..0xFC (or 0xF7..0xF9/0xFA..0xFC depending on needed data). - For humidity include 0xFD..0xFE. Data format: pressure and temperature are unsigned 20-bit values assembled from MSB, LSB, and XLSB nibbles (up[19:12]=0xF7, up[11:4]=0xF8, up[3:0]=0xF9[7:4]); temperature ut uses 0xFA..0xFC similarly; humidity is unsigned 16-bit uh formed from 0xFD (msb) and 0xFE (lsb). Shadowing: if a new measurement finishes while host is reading, new results are copied into shadow registers and will replace data registers only at end of burst read (CS rising for SPI or STOP condition for I2C). Side-effects: reading unused registers is faster than multiple small reads; recommended to do single burst reads to avoid inconsistent cross-sample mixing. Timing: reading is immediate; ensure host reads within constraints of interface timings. Error conditions: reading outside burst or using multiple sequential reads may return inconsistent multi-parameter sets when operating in normal mode.

device_functions.function_name: Read device status bits (measuring, im_update)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: none. Execution: read status register 0xF3. Register semantics: - measuring (0xF3[3]) is '1' whenever a conversion is running and '0' when results have been transferred to data registers. - im_update (0xF3[0]) is '1' while NVM trimming parameters are being copied to image registers (occurs at POR and before conversions) and '0' when copy finished. Use: poll measuring to know when measurement is complete (forced mode) or to detect safe times to change modes or ctrl_hum. Poll im_update after POR or reset to avoid reading calibration image while copying. Side-effects: read-only; no side-effects. Completion: when measuring==0 and im_update==0 device ready for writes/reads. Error: ignoring these bits may lead to race conditions (e.g., lost ctrl_hum update or inconsistent calibration usage).

device_functions.function_name: Compensate raw ADC to physical units (temperature, pressure, humidity)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must have read raw ADC values (20-bit pressure/temp, 16-bit humidity) from data registers and read trimming parameters (dig_*). Execution: compute compensated values using recommended formulas and intermediate t_fine. Temperature: compute t_fine from adc_T and dig_T1..T3; returns temperature (0.01°C resolution). Pressure: uses t_fine and dig_P1..P9; best accuracy requires 64-bit integer or double precision floating point; guard against var1==0 to avoid division by zero (return 0). Pressure output format: Q24.8 fixed point or Pa in double. Humidity: computed using t_fine and dig_H1..H6 with saturation and bounds (0..100% RH). Side-effects: no register writes; local software state variable t_fine must be retained between compensation calls for pressure/humidity. Error conditions: insufficient precision (32-bit alternative reduces accuracy and may add noise at high filter levels). Implementation notes: recommended to use Bosch API; if implementing, follow exact fixed-point sequences; check for over/underflow and saturate humidity to [0,100].

device_functions.function_name: Self-test flow (communication, bond-wire, and plausibility checks)
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must provide read/write/delay primitives. Execution sequence: 1) perform soft reset by writing 0xB6 to reset (0xE0) and wait ~2 ms; 2) read id (0xD0) and validate chip id==0x60; 3) read trimming parameters (0x88..0xA1, 0xE1..0xE7) and verify ranges; 4) configure sensor for a measurement (write ctrl_hum and ctrl_meas) and trigger a forced measurement, wait up to 7 ms for conversion (or poll status.measuring); 5) read uncompensated ADC and check for clipping to min/max ADC values (bond-wire test); 6) compute compensated temperature and pressure and compare against user-defined plausibility limits (e.g., 0..40°C, 900..1100 hPa). Register effects: writes to reset and ctrl_meas/ctrl_hum as part of test; reads from id, status, data, and calibration. Timing: total wait ~9 ms (2 ms reset + 7 ms conversion) plus communication time (dependent on interface speed). Return codes: defined codes for comm error, trimming out-of-bound, bond-wire failure, implausible temperature/pressure/humidity. Error semantics: tests performed in ascending code order; on first failing test the routine returns that code and stops further tests.

device_functions.function_name: Calculate measurement time, ODR and current consumption
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: host must know oversampling settings in ctrl_meas (osrs_t, osrs_p) and ctrl_hum (osrs_h) and t_sb in config. Execution: compute active measurement time using t_measure,typ and t_measure,max formulas: t_measure,typ = 1 + [2*T_oversampling]_{t!=0} + [2*P_oversampling + 0.5]_{p!=0} + [2*H_oversampling + 0.5]_{h!=0} (ms). Maximum similar with 2.3 factors. In forced mode max ODR = 1000 / t_measure. In normal mode ODR = 1000 / (t_measure + t_standby) where t_standby from config.t_sb. Current: compute I_DD,forced or I_DD,normal using formulas using I_DDSL, I_DDSB and per-measurement currents I_DDT, I_DDP, I_DDH multiplied by oversampling factors (see doc). Register dependencies: ctrl_meas (0xF4), ctrl_hum (0xF2), config.t_sb (0xF5[7:5]). Result: numerical ODR and expected average current consumption, used for power budgeting. Error semantics: t_standby accuracy subject to Δt_standby specification; actual current varies with temperature and oversampling selection.

device_functions.function_name: Interface selection and SPI/I²C access semantics
device_functions.function_description: Preconditions: physical CSB and SDO pin wiring determines active interface. Behavior: - If CSB tied to VDDIO the I²C interface is active. If CSB pulled low (asserted) the SPI interface becomes active and the device disables I²C until next POR. - SDO pin logic level selects LSB of I2C 7-bit address: SDO=GND -> 0x76, SDO=VDDIO -> 0x77; SDO must not be left floating. SPI specifics: MSB of SPI control byte is RW (1 for read, 0 for write); SPI register address uses 7 LSBs (i.e., SPI transfers use reg_addr without bit7) and auto-increment during multi-byte read/writes. 3-wire SPI is enabled by setting spi3w_en in config (0xF5[0]). I²C semantics: before reading, write register address in write mode then issue repeated-start and read; multi-byte reads auto-increment register address. Side-effects: pulling CSB low once locks device into SPI mode until POR. Timing: follow interface timing constraints in datasheet. Error conditions: leaving interface pins high when VDDIO is off can damage device via ESD diodes; ensure proper power sequencing. Note: spi3w_en controlled at config (0xF5) affects SDI/SDO pin behavior.
